lines: Good afternoon. I’m Hannah Thibedeau, and this is your Palindrome News brief.

A former United States Ambassador to Canada says he’s optimistic a bilateral deal between the two nations is looming but cautioned Canadians not to expect a Democrat-controlled Congress to reign in President Donald Trump’s tariffs, The Canadian Press reports.
Angine de Poitrine is extending its invasion of earth to the 2027 Grammy Awards, The Canadian Press reports.
The teachers of Ontario’s English Catholic schools have voted to give their union a strike mandate as negotiations with the government stall, The Canadian Press reports.
Three members of a Burlington family, including two children, have died following a house fire over the weekend, The Canadian Press reports.
Robert Pattinson is named the seventh James Bond, taking over from Daniel Craig, The Associated Press reports.

The Trump administration on Monday issued new rules to restrict remote access to advanced U.S. computing chips and servers, marking the latest step to limit China’s abilities to use U.S. chips to train their best artificial intelligence models, The Associated Press reports.
That’s your brief. We’ll keep watching, so you don’t have to.
